vc_fund_pitch.purpose: Create LP conviction in the fund thesis, track record, portfolio construction, pipeline, team, and terms.

arc: Prove that demand or usage exists.
Explain why this team and this financing plan can win.
repair_rules: If the slide has no proof, ask for evidence instead of inventing a metric.
If the slide repeats the previous slide, assign a sharper narrative job.

arc: Show why now is attractive for the strategy.
Prove sourcing, selection, and support advantage.
Show track record without overstating attribution.
Explain portfolio construction, terms, and current commitments.
repair_rules: Do not present unrealized marks as exits.
Separate thesis, process, pipeline, and terms into distinct jobs.

renderer_contract.instruction: The LLM must output render_schema_json only. The Svelte renderer converts schema elements to DOM.
forbidden: Do not output Tailwind utility classes.
Do not reference unverified external images.

bounds: Maintain at least 72px safe margin unless the element is a deliberate full-bleed background.
hierarchy: Use no more than 3 primary content groups.
Use contrast, spacing, and size before decoration.

claim_with_evidence.use_when: A slide needs one argument and 2-4 proof points.

two_column_before_after.use_when: Problem, solution, regulatory shift, or workflow comparison.
structure: Right: new state or unlocked opportunity
Bridge label that explains the change

metric_with_context.use_when: Traction, market, track record, pipeline, or economics.

matrix_or_map.use_when: Competition, positioning, portfolio construction, or blue ocean strategy.

visual_quality_bar: The slide can be understood in 5 seconds.
The visual structure reinforces the narrative job.
No decorative element competes with evidence.
Missing inputs are shown as conservative placeholders, not invented facts.

headline_rules: Avoid generic labels such as Problem, Solution, Market, or Traction when a stronger claim is possible.
Keep headlines under 16 words unless the source slide requires a longer legal or technical phrase.
evidence_rules: Use only facts present in deck context, source slides, uploaded artifacts, or user instruction.
If evidence is missing, ask for it or mark the claim as unverified.
Do not invent customer names, investor names, revenue, growth, clinical, regulatory, or financial metrics.

investor: Avoid hype unless the source material proves the claim.
lp: Precise about attribution, risk, liquidity, and terms.
operator: Show workflow consequence, speed, cost, and accountability.

proof_points.rule: Each point should include a claim and evidence or a missing-input note.

narrative_caption.rule: Explain why the visual matters, not what it literally shows.

risk_note.rule: State the caveat plainly when evidence is incomplete.

excellent: The slide has one clear narrative job.
The headline is a defensible claim grounded in supplied context.
The layout makes the main point visible before details.
The render schema is valid and bounded.
Missing evidence is surfaced honestly.
weak: The slide is a generic template with no project-specific judgment.
The headline is only a label.
The layout has too many competing groups.
The output invents metrics or customer proof.

excellent: The edit improves clarity while preserving source-backed facts.
The reason explains the investor or LP benefit.
Risk level reflects how much the edit changes meaning.
weak: The edit silently changes facts.
The edit adds unsupported claims.
The reason is generic.

excellent: The sequence feels like one argument.
Adjacent slides do different jobs.
The ask or next step is clear.
weak: Slides repeat the same claim.
Evidence appears before the audience understands why it matters.

hallucination_constraints.rule: Knowledge base content is structure, not user facts.
missing_input_behavior: Prefer a missing_inputs field over an invented detail.
Use conservative language when source support is weak.
Preserve original source facts exactly unless the user supplied a correction.

sequence.purpose: Establish company identity and one-line promise.
Make the pain clear and urgent.
Show the company's answer to the problem.
Show the opportunity is large and reachable.
Show proof of demand, even if early.
Explain how the company captures value.
Show why this company can win.
Explain why this team is credible.

conditional_rules.action: Do not fabricate traction. Use milestones, pilots, LOIs, waitlist, or learning velocity only if provided.
Add technical defensibility after product or before competition when source material supports it.

sequence.purpose: Show why this fund has a differentiated edge.
Explain why the team can execute the thesis.
Make fund economics and structure explicit.

conditional_rules.action: Do not imply realized returns. Use relevant operating, angel, scout, or unrealized evidence with caveats.
Mark pipeline as unverified and request deal-stage evidence.

hallucination_rules.rule: If traction metrics are missing, do not invent revenue, users, customers, pilots, LOIs, growth rate, retention, or pipeline.
hallucination_rules.fallback: Return missing_inputs and suggest acceptable proof types.

hallucination_rules.rule: Do not claim a regulatory approval, mandate, enforcement action, or policy deadline unless present in source context.
hallucination_rules.fallback: Frame as a possible regulatory angle and request source evidence.

hallucination_rules.rule: Do not invent MOIC, DPI, IRR, exit values, portfolio company names, or attribution.
hallucination_rules.fallback: Use a missing-input warning and request verified fund data.

smart_edit_rules.rule: A Smart Edit may improve clarity, tone, and structure, but it must not silently change facts.
smart_edit_rules.risk_level: high when the edit changes numbers, names, legal claims, or causal claims

smart_edit_rules.rule: Every Smart Edit reason should explain how the edit helps investor, LP, buyer, or operator understanding.
If an edit needs proof that is absent, mention the missing input rather than adding the proof.

rules: sourceFactsUsed must list only facts present in selected source slides, deck artifacts, or user instruction.
assumptions must be explicit and conservative.
missingInputs must be non-empty when required evidence is absent.
qualityWarnings must explain any weak evidence, unclear claim, or layout risk.
confidence must be between 0 and 1 and should decrease when evidence is missing.

archetypes.title: Blue Ocean Strategy
archetypes.description: Positioning via the Strategy Canvas from Kim & Mauborgne's Blue Ocean Strategy — diagrams the team's value curve against incumbents using the ERIC (Eliminate, Reduce, Raise, Create) framework.
archetypes.body_md: A structured alternative or companion to `positioning`. Where `positioning` argues differentiation in prose, the Strategy Canvas argues it visually: a value-curve chart over category factors, with the ERIC delta — which factors the team *Eliminates*, *Reduces*, *Raises*, and *Creates* relative to incumbents. Most often used by startups breaking from category conventions; occasionally by emerging managers showing how their fund repositions versus peer funds.

archetypes.title: Why Now
archetypes.description: The market-timing argument — what changed in the world (tech, regulation, behavior, cost curve) that makes this the moment for the bet.
archetypes.body_md: Shared archetype. Distinct from `problem` (which is about pain) and `market-size` (which is about scale) — `why-now` is about timing: the inflection that makes this the right window. In a startup deck it rides between problem and solution; in a VC deck it rides between fund-thesis and the credibility slides.
